label: answerable
question: My landlord wants 15% more rent when I renew. I pay AED 80,000 a year and the rental index average for similar flats is AED 100,000. Is he allowed?
reference_answer: No. The rent is 20% below the average, which falls in the 11%-20% band of Decree 43/2013 Art. 1(b), so the maximum increase is 5% (AED 4,000, i.e. AED 84,000). A 15% increase exceeds the cap.

quotes.text: five percent (5%) of the Rent of the Real Property unit, where the Rent is eleven percent (11%) to twenty percent (20%) less than the average rental value of similar units

label: answerable
question: rent is 50000 and average in area 52000, landlord can increase or not?
reference_answer: No increase is allowed. The rent is only about 3.8% below the average, and Decree 43/2013 Art. 1(a) allows no increase where the rent is up to 10% below the average rental value of similar units.

quotes.text: no Rent increase, where the Rent of the Real Property unit is up to ten percent (10%) less than the average rental value of similar units

label: answerable
question: My annual rent is AED 60,000 and the average rent for similar units is AED 100,000. What is the maximum my landlord can increase the rent by at renewal?
reference_answer: Up to 15% (AED 9,000). The rent is exactly 40% below the average, which is in the 31%-40% band of Decree 43/2013 Art. 1(d).

quotes.text: fifteen percent (15%) of the Rent of the Real Property unit, where the Rent is thirty-one percent (31%) to forty percent (40%) less than the average rental value of similar units

label: answerable
question: I'm paying 55k but similar apartments go for 100k. How much can my rent go up?
reference_answer: Up to 20% (AED 11,000). The rent is 45% below the average, i.e. more than 40% below, which is the top band of Decree 43/2013 Art. 1(e).

quotes.text: twenty percent (20%) of the Rent of the Real Property Unit, where the Rent is more than forty percent (40%) less than the average rental value of similar units

label: answerable
question: How is the 'average rent of similar units' decided when working out whether my rent can be increased?
reference_answer: Decree 43/2013 Art. 3 says the average rental value of similar units is determined by the official Rent Index of the Emirate of Dubai. Since 2 January 2025 that index is DLD's Smart Rental Index, which values each building using a building classification system (technical condition, finishes, location, services).

quotes.text: the average rental value of similar units will be determined in accordance with the "Rent Index of the Emirate of Dubai" approved by the Real Estate Regulatory Agency

label: partially_answerable
question: Does the rent increase cap also apply to landlords in free zones like DIFC?
reference_answer: Decree 43/2013 Art. 2 states it applies to all landlords in Dubai, including special development zones and free zones such as DIFC. However, DLD states the Smart Rental Index covers free zones but excludes DIFC, so how the benchmark is set for DIFC units is not answered by the corpus; DIFC questions should be escalated.

quotes.text: including those in Special Development zones and free zones such as the Dubai International Financial Centre

label: answerable
question: My contract ends on 1 December 2026 and the landlord told me on 1 November 2026 that the rent is going up. Is that valid notice?
reference_answer: No, unless your contract says otherwise. Art. 14 of Law 26/2007 (as amended) requires a party wishing to change the terms, including the rent, to notify the other at least 90 days before expiry. Notice given 30 days before expiry is too late.

quotes.text: that party must notify the other party of this intent no less than ninety (90) days before the date on which the Lease Contract expires

label: answerable
question: I want ask landlord to reduce the rent when renewal. How many days before I must tell him?
reference_answer: The 90-day rule applies to either party: unless agreed otherwise, the tenant must notify the landlord at least 90 days before the contract expires (Art. 14). Art. 13 allows the parties to reconsider increasing or reducing the rent before expiry.

quotes.text: where either party wishes to amend any of its terms pursuant to Article (13) of this Law

original_question: As a tenant, if I want to ask for lower rent or different terms at renewal, how much notice must I give?

label: answerable
question: My lease ended last month but I just kept living there and paying, nobody said anything. What happens to my contract now?
reference_answer: Under Art. 6, if the tenant stays on without objection from the landlord, the contract is renewed for the same term or one year, whichever is shorter, on the same terms as before.

quotes.text: the Lease Contract will be renewed for the same term or for a term of one year, whichever is shorter, and under the same terms as the previous Lease Contract

label: answerable
question: me and landlord not agreeing on new rent for renewal, who will decide the rent then?
reference_answer: The Tribunal (today the Rental Disputes Center) may determine the fair rent, applying the Art. 9 criteria such as RERA's increase criteria, the economic situation, the property's condition and rents of similar property (Art. 13).

quotes.text: If the Landlord and Tenant fail to reach an agreement in this regard, the Tribunal may determine the fair Rent, taking into account the criteria stipulated in Article (9) of this Law

original_question: If my landlord and I cannot agree on the new rent at renewal, who decides?

question: The building I live in was sold to a new owner. Do I have to move out?
reference_answer: No. Under Art. 28 a transfer of ownership does not affect the tenant's right to stay under the lease made with the previous owner, provided the lease has a fixed term.

quotes.text: Transferring the ownership of Real Property to a new owner does not affect the Tenant's right to continue to occupy the Real Property by virtue of the Lease Contract entered into with the previous owner, provided that such Lease Contract has a fixed term

label: answerable
question: My landlord wants to sell the flat. Can he make me leave when my lease ends?
reference_answer: Yes, sale is one of the grounds for eviction at expiry (Art. 25(2)(d), as amended), but the landlord must give at least 12 months' notice of the eviction reason, served through a notary public or by registered mail.

quotes.text: the leased Real Property owner wishes to sell it
the Landlord must notify the Tenant of the eviction reasons at least twelve (12) months before the date of eviction, and the notice must be served through a Notary Public or by registered mail

label: answerable
question: Landlord sent me a WhatsApp message saying I must vacate in 12 months because his son is moving in. Is that enough?
reference_answer: Not as described. Own use by a first-degree relative is a ground for eviction at expiry (Art. 25(2)(c)), and 12 months is the right period, but the notice must be served through a notary public or by registered mail, so a WhatsApp message does not satisfy Art. 25. The landlord must also prove he owns no other suitable property.

quotes.text: the Real Property owner wishes to retake possession of the Real Property for his own use or for use by any of his first-degree relatives, provided that the owner proves that he does not own any alternative Real Property that is suitable for this purpose
the notice must be served through a Notary Public or by registered mail

label: answerable
question: If my landlord evicts me saying he needs the apartment for himself, can he rent it to someone else straight away?
reference_answer: No. Under Art. 26 (as amended) he may not rent a residential property to a third party for at least two years after retaking possession; otherwise the tenant can ask the Tribunal for fair compensation.

quotes.text: the Landlord may not rent the Real Property to a third party before the lapse of at least two (2) years in case of residential Real Property

label: answerable
question: My building is going to be demolished and rebuilt. Do I have any right to come back afterwards?
reference_answer: Yes. Art. 29 gives the tenant a right of first refusal to return to a demolished-and-reconstructed or renovated property, at a rent set under Art. 9, but it must be exercised within 30 days of being notified by the landlord.

quotes.text: A Tenant will have the right of first refusal to return to the Real Property where it is demolished and reconstructed, or renovated and restored, by the Landlord
within a period not exceeding thirty (30) days from the date on which the Tenant is notified of the same by the Landlord

label: answerable
question: The landlord says the building needs major renovation and I have to leave. What does the law require?
reference_answer: Major restoration is a ground for eviction only at the expiry of the lease (Art. 25(2)(b)). The condition must be verified by a technical report issued or certified by Dubai Municipality, and the landlord must give 12 months' notice through a notary public or registered mail.

quotes.text: the Real Property is in a condition that requires restoration or comprehensive maintenance that cannot be carried out while the Tenant occupies the Real Property, provided that this condition of the Real Property is verified by a technical report issued or certified by the Dubai Municipality

label: answerable
question: I am late in rent payment, how much time landlord must give me before he can evict me?
reference_answer: Unless otherwise agreed, the landlord must first serve a notice requesting payment through a notary public or by registered mail; only if the rent is not paid within 30 days of that notice can he request eviction (Art. 25(1)(a)). Eviction itself requires a ruling.

quotes.text: where the Tenant fails to pay the Rent or any part thereof within thirty (30) days from the date of service of a Notice on the Tenant by the Landlord requesting the payment

original_question: I'm behind on rent. How fast can my landlord kick me out?

question: Can my landlord end my contract halfway through because he wants the flat for his daughter?
reference_answer: No. A valid lease cannot be ended unilaterally during its term (Art. 7). Use by the owner or a first-degree relative is a ground only upon expiry, with 12 months' notice (Art. 25(2)(c)); it is not one of the during-term grounds in Art. 25(1).

quotes.text: it may not be unilaterally terminated during its term by the Landlord or the Tenant

label: answerable
question: I rented out my spare room without telling the landlord. What can happen?
reference_answer: Unless otherwise agreed, subletting needs the landlord's written consent (Art. 24). Subletting any part without written approval is a ground for eviction during the term, and the eviction applies to both you and the subtenant (Art. 25(1)(b)).

quotes.text: the Tenant may not assign the use of or sub-lease the Real Property to third parties unless written consent of the Landlord is obtained
where the Tenant sublets the Real Property or any part thereof without obtaining the Landlord's written approval

label: answerable
question: If I break a term of my lease, does my landlord have to warn me before trying to evict me?
reference_answer: Yes. For breach of an obligation or contract term, the landlord must serve a notice (through a notary public or registered mail) and can only seek eviction if the tenant fails to comply within 30 days (Art. 25(1)(h)).

quotes.text: where the Tenant fails to comply with any of his obligations under this Law or any of the Lease Contract terms within thirty (30) days from the date on which a Notice requesting him to comply with that obligation or term is served upon him by the Landlord

label: answerable
question: Can I be evicted before my lease ends if the building is unsafe?
reference_answer: Yes, if the property is likely to collapse, but the landlord must prove it with a technical report issued or certified by Dubai Municipality (Art. 25(1)(g)).

quotes.text: where the Real Property is likely to collapse, provided that the Landlord proves this by a technical report issued by or certified by the Dubai Municipality

label: answerable
question: AC not working in my flat and landlord saying I have to pay for repair. Is it correct?
reference_answer: Unless the contract says otherwise, the landlord is responsible during the lease for maintenance and for repairing defects that affect the tenant's intended use (Art. 16), and for wear and tear not caused by the tenant's fault (Art. 17).

quotes.text: Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the Landlord will, during the term of the Lease Contract, be responsible for the Real Property' maintenance works and for repairing any defect or damage that may affect the Tenant's intended use of the Real Property

original_question: The AC in my apartment broke down. Who has to pay for the repair, me or the landlord?

question: Can I renovate or make changes to my apartment myself?
reference_answer: Only with the landlord's permission and after obtaining the required licences (Art. 19). Where you have permission for decoration works that need official approvals and do not affect the structure, the landlord must provide the approvals you need (Art. 18).

quotes.text: the Tenant may not make any changes or carry out any restoration or maintenance works to the Real Property unless so permitted by the Landlord and after obtaining required licences from the competent official entities

label: answerable
question: I need official approvals for some works in my flat but the landlord refuses to give me the documents. What can I do?
reference_answer: Art. 18 obliges the landlord to provide the approvals needed for decoration or other works that do not affect the structure. If he refuses, the tenant can file a case at the Rental Disputes Centre asking that he be compelled to provide them, showing the works do not affect the structure.

quotes.text: The Landlord must provide the Tenant with the approvals required to be submitted to the competent official entities in the Emirate whenever the Tenant wishes to carry out decoration works

label: answerable
question: When I move out, do I have to fix small scratches on the walls from normal living?
reference_answer: No. You must return the property in the condition you received it, except for ordinary wear and tear or damage beyond your control (Art. 21). Disputes are decided by the Tribunal.

quotes.text: except for ordinary wear and tear or for damage due to reasons beyond the Tenant's control

label: answerable
question: Is my landlord legally required to take a security deposit, and is there a maximum amount?
reference_answer: Art. 20 says the landlord 'may' take a security deposit to ensure maintenance and must refund it (or the remainder) at expiry. The law does not set a maximum amount. (Some DLD/RDC guidance describes the deposit as mandatory; the law itself says 'may'.)

quotes.text: the Landlord may obtain from the Tenant a security deposit to ensure maintenance of the Real Property upon the expiry of the Lease Contract

label: answerable
question: landlord not giving back my deposit money, flat i left clean and good condition. what i can do?
reference_answer: The landlord must refund the deposit or its remainder at expiry (Art. 20). The RDC states a tenant can recover the deposit by filing a Payment Writ and requesting a refund; disputes about the condition of the property go to the Tribunal (Art. 21).

quotes.text: provided that the Landlord undertakes to refund such deposit or remainder thereof to the Tenant upon the expiry of the Lease Contract
You can secure the return of your security deposit by submitting a Payment Writ and requesting a refund.

original_question: My landlord won't give back my deposit even though I left the flat in good condition. What can I do?

label: answerable
question: Can the landlord deduct repair costs from my security deposit?
reference_answer: The deposit exists to ensure maintenance of the property at expiry, and the landlord must refund the deposit 'or remainder thereof', so deductions for damage the tenant caused are contemplated; ordinary wear and tear is excluded from the tenant's responsibility (Art. 21).

quotes.text: refund such deposit or remainder thereof

label: answerable
question: when i can take back my security deposit money?
reference_answer: At the expiry of the lease, provided the property is returned in the condition it was received (apart from normal wear and tear). The landlord must refund the deposit or its remainder then (Art. 20).

quotes.text: refund such deposit or remainder thereof to the Tenant upon the expiry of the Lease Contract

label: answerable
question: Is it compulsory to register my tenancy contract (Ejari)?
reference_answer: Yes. All lease contracts for property governed by the law, and any amendments, must be registered with RERA (Art. 4(2), as amended); Ejari is DLD's system for that registration.

quotes.text: All Lease Contracts related to Real Property which is governed by the provisions of this Law, and any amendments thereto, will be registered with RERA

label: answerable
question: Can I register the Ejari myself as the tenant or does the landlord have to do it?
reference_answer: A tenant can start the Ejari registration (via the Dubai REST app, or at a trustee office with an NOC from the owner), but the landlord's approval is required to complete it.

quotes.text: a tenant can initiate the registration of the Ejari contract, but the landlord's approval is required for the process to be completed

label: answerable
question: How much does it cost to register an Ejari contract through the Dubai REST app?
reference_answer: AED 177.75 in total: AED 100 registration, AED 10 knowledge fee, AED 10 innovation fee, and a service partner fee of AED 55 plus VAT.

quotes.text: Total: 177.75 AED

label: answerable
question: last year i did not do ejari. now renewal time, can i do ejari only for this year?
reference_answer: No. DLD states a lease cannot be registered in Ejari if previous contracts were not registered; missed earlier registrations must be registered first.

quotes.text: it is not possible to register a lease contract with Ejari if the previous contracts are not registered already

original_question: I never registered Ejari last year. Can I just register this year's renewal?

question: What documents do I need to register a tenancy contract at a real estate trustee centre?
reference_answer: The original unified tenancy contract, the applicant's UAE ID, and an official power of attorney if the applicant is acting for someone else.

quotes.text: 1- The original unified tenancy contract

label: answerable
question: I got cheaper flat, can I leave my flat before contract finish?
reference_answer: Not unilaterally. A valid lease can only be terminated during its term by mutual consent or under the provisions of the law (Art. 7). Early termination depends on a clause in your contract or agreement with the landlord.

quotes.text: It can only be terminated by mutual consent or in accordance with the provisions of this Law

original_question: I found a cheaper place. Can I just break my lease and leave early?

label: partially_answerable
question: How many months of rent is the penalty for ending my lease early?
reference_answer: The corpus sets no statutory early-termination penalty. Termination during the term requires mutual consent or a legal ground (Art. 7); DLD says early-termination terms depend on the tenancy agreement or negotiation with the landlord.

quotes.text: Unless there is a provision in your tenancy agreement for early termination, it is subject to discussion and agreement between the landlord and the tenant

label: answerable
question: If a tenant dies, does the tenancy contract end?
reference_answer: No. The lease continues with the heirs, who may terminate it by giving the landlord at least 30 days' notice, or it ends at expiry if that comes first (Art. 27).

quotes.text: The Lease Contract does not expire upon the death of the Landlord or the Tenant

label: answerable
question: Do I need my landlord's permission to sublease part of my apartment?
reference_answer: Yes, unless the lease says otherwise, the tenant needs the landlord's written consent to sublease or assign the use of the property (Art. 24).

quotes.text: unless written consent of the Landlord is obtained

label: answerable
question: I'm a subtenant. What happens to my sublease if the main tenant's lease ends?
reference_answer: The sublease expires when the main lease expires unless the landlord expressly agrees to extend it (Art. 8). If the Tribunal terminates the main lease and the sublease was approved by the landlord, the subtenant may continue under the sublease terms (Art. 30).

quotes.text: will expire upon the expiry of the term of the Lease Contract entered into between the Landlord and Tenant, unless the Landlord expressly agrees to extend the term of the sub-lease contract

label: answerable
question: landlord is not taking my rent cheque on purpose so he can say i not paid. what to do?
reference_answer: Deposit the rent with the Rental Disputes Centre's treasury using an 'offer and deposit' request; the centre notifies the landlord, and once the judge accepts the request you are treated as having paid from that date.

quotes.text: The tenant is obliged to deposit the rent into the Rental Disputes Centre's treasury

original_question: My landlord is refusing to take my rent so he can say I didn't pay. What should I do?

question: My contract doesn't say when rent is due. How must I pay it?
reference_answer: Where no payment dates were agreed or they cannot be proven, the annual rent is payable in four equal instalments in advance (Art. 12).

quotes.text: the Rent must be annually paid in four (4) equal instalments to be paid in advance

question: My rent cheque bounced. What can the landlord do through the RDC?
reference_answer: The landlord can apply for a Payment Writ (documents include the cheque return memo and proof of notice to the debtor); the debtor must be notified through a notary public or registered mail and given five days. Non-payment can also ground eviction after a 30-day payment notice (Art. 25(1)(a)). Criminal aspects of bounced cheques are outside the corpus.

quotes.text: Cheque return memo issued by the relevant bank
The defendant's notification through a notary public or registered mail, followed by a period of five days.

question: How much will it cost to file a rent dispute at the RDC if my annual rent is AED 90,000?
reference_answer: The registration fee is 3.5% of the annual rent, i.e. AED 3,150 (within the AED 500 minimum and AED 20,000 maximum), plus fixed charges of AED 100 process service, AED 10 knowledge fee and AED 10 innovation fee (and AED 25 if a power of attorney is registered).

quotes.text: Fee not less than (AED 500) and not more than (AED 20,000)

question: My villa rent is AED 700,000 a year. What is the RDC filing fee for an eviction dispute?
reference_answer: 3.5% of AED 700,000 would be AED 24,500, but the fee is capped at AED 20,000, so the filing fee is AED 20,000 plus the fixed charges.

quotes.text: not more than (AED 20,000)

question: my room rent only 10000 per year, how much fee for rental dispute case?
reference_answer: 3.5% of AED 10,000 is AED 350, which is below the minimum, so the filing fee is the minimum of AED 500 plus the fixed charges.

quotes.text: Fee not less than (AED 500)

question: If my landlord and I settle the dispute through mediation, do I get any of the RDC fee back?
reference_answer: Yes. If conciliation leads to a settlement, half of the court fee paid for basic claims is refunded.

quotes.text: half of the court fee paid for basic claims is refunded

question: RDC gave judgment against me, how many days i have for appeal?
reference_answer: 15 days from the day after the hearing at which the judgment was issued, or from service of the judgment if you never appeared. For financial claims the judgment debtor must deposit half of the judgment amount to have the appeal admitted (D26/2013 Art. 18).

quotes.text: The time limit for appeal of a judgment issued by the First Instance Division is fifteen (15) days from the day following the date of the hearing in which the judgment was issued

question: Can every RDC judgment be appealed?
reference_answer: No. Judgments in rent claims worth less than AED 100,000 are final, except in listed cases such as an eviction judgment or breach of jurisdiction rules (D26/2013 Art. 17). Appellate judgments are final (Art. 14).

quotes.text: with the exception of judgments issued in rent claims whose value is less than one hundred thousand Dirhams (AED 100,000.00), which will be final and not subject to any form of appeal

label: answerable
question: My landlord cut off the electricity and water to pressure me to leave. Is that allowed?
reference_answer: No. The landlord may not disconnect services or disturb the tenant's use (Art. 34). The tenant can go to the police station with jurisdiction over the property to seek a remedy or file a report, and can claim damages before the Tribunal supported by official reports.

quotes.text: The Landlord may not disconnect services from the Real Property or disturb the Tenant in his use of the Real Property in any manner

question: What documents do I need to file a case at the Rental Disputes Center?
reference_answer: Including: a copy of the latest lease contract (Ejari), Emirates ID (and trade licence for companies), the owner's passport/residence and Emirates ID where relevant, a valid management contract where applicable, and a bank letter or statement with the claimant's IBAN.

quotes.text: 1- A copy of the last lease contract (Ejari).
